sources.publisher: Altarea SCA
sources.source_family: Altarea press releases and regulated information
sources.summary: Altarea's third-quarter business release, dated Paris 21 October 2026, has a section 'Nouvelles avancées en Data centers'. It reports that during the quarter Altarea fully let its proximity data centre at Noyal (Rennes), of 3 MW IT, and that the group launched works this summer on a 7 MW IT data centre at Vélizy-Villacoublay (Yvelines), to meet the timetables of clients with whom advanced discussions are under way, with delivery of the site to its user expected within 18 months. The summary page headlines the full letting of Noyal and the 'première pierre' (first stone) of the 7 MW IT Vélizy project.
sources.date_semantics: Release dated 21 October 2026 (cover line 'Paris, le 21 octobre 2026, 17h35'; PDF created the same day). Its financial data are stated at 30 September 2026; the data-centre statements describe the quarter and the position at publication. The launch of works is dated only to 'this summer' and the first-stone ceremony is not dated, so neither is used as an observation day; the 18-month delivery is a forecast.

sources.date_semantics: Release dated 29 July 2026; the business report describes the position at 30 June 2026. Used as context for identity and earlier status only; the 21 October 2026 release is the status source. Commissioning timings are forecasts.

sources.title: IIJ concludes disaster power-supply agreement with Matsue City using the batteries installed at the IIJ Matsue Data Center Park (press release, 5 October 2026)
sources.publisher: Internet Initiative Japan Inc.
sources.capture_note: Captured 22 October 2026 (20,438 bytes) after www.iij.ad.jp robots.txt was read (HTTP 404, no rules); rehashed against its metadata before use. The release's own PDF (iij-20261005-matsue.pdf, sha256 21a16071...ff8b, 935,968 bytes) carries the same text. Only a compact factual paraphrase is recorded; the raw files are not redistributed.
sources.summary: IIJ's release of 5 October 2026 announces that IIJ concluded, that day, a disaster power-supply agreement with Matsue City. Under it IIJ will use the large-capacity lithium-ion batteries and EV chargers installed at its IIJ Matsue Data Center Park (Matsue DCP) to supply two municipal community centres used as evacuation shelters, reserving about 1,000 kWh for the city. The release states that the installed batteries are operated as backup power for the data-centre facilities and are used for the shelters in a disaster, and that in normal times they also support local demand-response requests. It describes the existing Matsue DCP; it gives no new building, phase, capacity, construction, pause or closure.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 2026年10月5日 on the release and its PDF; the agreement was concluded the same day. 5 October 2026 is used as the observation day of the existing Matsue DCP's continuing operations as described by its operator. It is not an opening, commissioning or inspection date, and the planned disaster drills are future work that is not used.

sources.title: Plainsmen Holdings, LLC: Application 2, rezone West Campus western quarter (SW/4 Section 16, T22N, R6W) from A to I-3 - Project Thunderbird
sources.publisher: City of Enid, Oklahoma (application filed by Plainsmen Holdings, LLC)
sources.attribution: City of Enid, Oklahoma, Community Development Department; applicant Plainsmen Holdings, LLC
sources.summary: Rezoning application received by the City of Enid on 27 August 2026 (date stamp on the application page, 'Page 19 of 46' of the combined North and West package). It asks to rezone the West Campus western quarter, the Southwest Quarter of Section 16, Township 22 North, Range 6 West of the Indian Meridian, Garfield County, within the Enid corporate limits, less a 183 by 187 ft tract at its southwest corner, from 'A' Agricultural (General) to 'I-3' Industrial (Heavy). Item 4 states that if rezoned the property will be used for heavy industrial use 'which may include data center and associated support facilities' and that no electric generating facility is proposed on this property. The legal owner is Two Boots Land and Cattle, LLC; the applicant and signatory is Plainsmen Holdings, LLC. The cover letter describes three coordinated applications for the North and West campuses under common development. The applicant's area map is titled 'Project Thunderbird - Area Map' and shows the tract between S 16th St and S 30th St north of E Rupe Ave. The package also reproduces the 30 March 2026 deed to the owner (recorded 2 April 2026, Book 2751, Pages 723-727).
sources.date_semantics: Filing date of a rezoning application (regulatory filing to the municipal planning authority), from the City's received stamp and the City's Project Thunderbird page ('Submitted Aug. 27, 2026'). It is an application, not a consent; it does not authorise any data-centre development. The package contains names, signatures and contact details of private individuals (agent, notary, neighbouring owners in the certified 300-foot list, deed parties); none is restated.
sources.personal_data_note: Private individuals' names, phone numbers and e-mail addresses printed in the package are not copied.

sources.title: Enid Natives Unveil Project Thunderbird: A Long-Term Investment in Economic Growth and National Security (Plainsmen Holdings, LLC press release)
sources.publisher: Plainsmen Holdings, LLC (applicant material hosted by the City of Enid)
sources.summary: Plainsmen Holdings, LLC announced plans to develop Project Thunderbird, 'a data center and power corridor infrastructure initiative' in Enid and Garfield County. The proposed development encompasses approximately 1,735 acres across four campuses in Enid and includes plans for an on-site power generation facility of up to 3.3 gigawatts through a partnership with an unnamed natural gas midstream provider; the project would use raw water from the Kaw Lake Pipeline and closed-loop cooling. A related Patriot Utility District would provide backup power and fiber for Vance Air Force Base. The release says further details will be announced; it names no campus tract, IT capacity, operator or schedule.
sources.date_semantics: Release dated 7 September 2026 under embargo until 8 September 2026, 10 a.m. CST; the City of Enid page lists it as 'Posted Sept. 8, 2026. Provided by the project representative, not the City.' The 3.3 GW figure is planned on-site generation, not IT load. Media contacts and principals are private individuals and are not restated.
